## Precipitation and evaporation kinetics in the example drivers (driver-level coupling) {#sec-ch10-kinetics}

Local symbols: $\dot{\boldsymbol\omega}$ is the vector of reaction rates [$\mathrm{mol\,m^{-3}\,s^{-1}}$] and
$\mathsf J_{\dot\omega}$ its Jacobian with respect to the molar concentrations; $x$ is the extent of a
two-product evaporation to equilibrium [$\mathrm{mol\,m^{-3}}$]. Tracked in ISSUES.md. The subscript keeps
$\mathsf J_{\dot\omega}$ apart from the $\mathsf J$ of the phase solve in @sec-ch02-saturation.

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**What it does.** Between two steps, advances the species by one linearised backward-Euler step of kintera's
reaction rates (evaporation, precipitation), then asks `check_redo` whether to keep the step.
**Switch.** None in the library: it runs only in drivers that build a kintera `Kinetics` from the card.
**Changes.** Species rows only; $E$ is untouched. **Order.** First order in time.
**Defining equation.** @eq-ch10-kinetics-step.
:::

The snapy library does not run reaction kinetics. Two example drivers do: `examples/run_hydro.cpp` and
`examples/jupiter_evap_precip_1d.cpp`. After all RK stages of a step, they refresh the primitive state, evaluate
kintera's rates and their Jacobian at the post-step state, take one linearised implicit step for the
concentrations, add the change to the species rows of the conserved state and call `check_redo`. The coupling is
therefore operator-split, first order, and a property of those drivers: a run built on the library alone has no
kinetics unless its own driver adds the same block. As with the saturation adjustment, latent heat is carried by
the reference energies, so the energy row is not touched.

Aliases: the refresh before kinetics is #257 ([chengcli/snapy#257](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/issues/257));
the two-product extent law is kintera #114.

### Derivation

The rates are evaluated once, at the concentrations $\tilde{\mathbf c}$ of the step's end. Linearising
$\dot{\boldsymbol\omega}$ about them and taking one backward-Euler step of
$\mathrm{d}\tilde{\mathbf c}/\mathrm{d}t=\mathsf N\dot{\boldsymbol\omega}(\tilde{\mathbf c})$ gives

$$
\Big(\frac{\mathsf I}{\Delta t}-\mathsf N\mathsf J_{\dot\omega}\Big)\Delta\tilde{\mathbf c} = \mathsf N\dot{\boldsymbol\omega}
$$ {#eq-ch10-kinetics-step}

for the change $\Delta\tilde{\mathbf c}$ over the step $\Delta t$. @eq-ch10-kinetics-step is assembled as `A` and
`sr` in `evolve_implicit_cell`
([`kintera evolve_implicit_impl.h:66-71`](https://github.com/chengcli/kintera/blob/c55b13b2204997d2d09e04498558ab9495d8ee77/src/kinetics/evolve_implicit_impl.h#L66-L71), `inv_dt`)
and solved by LU with partial pivoting, falling back to a minimum-norm least-squares solve for a singular cell
([`kintera evolve_implicit_impl.h:77`](https://github.com/chengcli/kintera/blob/c55b13b2204997d2d09e04498558ab9495d8ee77/src/kinetics/evolve_implicit_impl.h#L77), `dsolve_lu`).
For a linear rate law the step is exactly backward Euler (check line `[C2]`). For the reversible linear reaction
$A\rightleftharpoons B$ with rate constants $k_{\mathrm f}$, $k_{\mathrm b}$ it moves the distance to equilibrium by
the factor $1/(1+\Delta t(k_{\mathrm f}+k_{\mathrm b}))$, which lies in $(0,1]$ for every $\Delta t$: one step never
overshoots equilibrium, however large the step (`[C3]`). The driver converts the change to partial densities,
$\Delta\rho_n=\mu_n\Delta\tilde c_n$; for a mass-balanced reaction $\sum_n\mu_n\nu_{nk}=0$, so the update has zero net
mass (`[C4]`).

For a condensate evaporating into two gases, $AB(s)\to A+B$, kintera's rate is proportional to the extent $x$ that
would bring the gases to equilibrium, the positive root of $(\tilde c_A+x)(\tilde c_B+x)=K$. The code evaluates it
in a form without cancellation,

$$
x = \frac{2\,(K-\tilde c_A\tilde c_B)}{\tilde c_A+\tilde c_B+\sqrt{(\tilde c_A-\tilde c_B)^2+4K}},
$$ {#eq-ch10-kinetics-extent}

and sets it to zero for supersaturated cells. @eq-ch10-kinetics-extent is computed as `x` in
`EvaporationImpl::forward`
([`kintera evaporation.cpp:180-191`](https://github.com/chengcli/kintera/blob/c55b13b2204997d2d09e04498558ab9495d8ee77/src/kinetics/evaporation.cpp#L180-L191), `root`).
`[C1]` shows symbolically that it is the positive root. The full derivation of the steady-diffusion rate law behind
it is in `sources/canoe__EVAPORATION_MULTIPRODUCT_TECH_REPORT.md` section 4, written in symbols this report reserves for
other quantities; its translation into the report's notation is still to be written.

### Numerical method

The block runs once per accepted or attempted step, after the stages and before `check_redo`
([`run_hydro.cpp:171-195`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/examples/run_hydro.cpp#L171-L195)).
It first recomputes `hydro_w` from `hydro_u`, so the rates see the saturation-adjusted state
([`run_hydro.cpp:175-176`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/examples/run_hydro.cpp#L175-L176)).
It acts on the whole array, ghosts included, with no exchange; the next stage's boundary fill and exchange restore
consistency. No conserved limiter runs between the update and `check_redo`, so a negative species produced by the
kinetics shows up as a limiter repair, and possibly a redo, at the next step. @fig-ch10-kinetics-extent compares
the extent law with the earlier law $K-\tilde c_A\tilde c_B$.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch10-kinetics-extent
#| fig-cap: "Evaporation drive of a two-product condensate against the saturation ratio, each curve divided by its value at zero saturation. Green: the extent law, solid for equal gas concentrations, dashed for one gas ten times the other; blue dotted: the earlier law $K-\\tilde c_A\\tilde c_B$. The extent law falls faster near zero saturation, and depends on how the product is split between the gases."
#| fig-alt: "Three decreasing curves from 1 at saturation ratio 0 to 0 at ratio 1; the two extent curves lie below the straight dotted line."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch10.fig_kinetics_extent import make_fig
make_fig()
```

: Code map of the driver-level kinetics. {#tbl-ch10-kinetics-code}

1. Refresh the primitives from the adjusted conserved state ([`run_hydro.cpp:175-176`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/examples/run_hydro.cpp#L175-L176), `hydro_w`).
2. Form temperature, pressure and concentrations ([`run_hydro.cpp:177-181`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/examples/run_hydro.cpp#L177-L181), `conc`).
3. Evaluate rates and Jacobian ([`run_hydro.cpp:184-186`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/examples/run_hydro.cpp#L184-L186), `jacobian`).
4. Take the implicit step and convert to densities ([`run_hydro.cpp:187-190`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/examples/run_hydro.cpp#L187-L190), `del_rho`).
5. Add to the species rows ([`run_hydro.cpp:191`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/examples/run_hydro.cpp#L191), `hydro_u`).
6. Accept, redo or terminate ([`run_hydro.cpp:193-195`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/examples/run_hydro.cpp#L193-L195), `check_redo`).

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_uranus_cycle1_abort.release` | column reaches cycle 40, no redo | exit status | log strings |

: Tests of the driver-level kinetics; assertions read from the test sources at the pin, not run. {#tbl-ch10-kinetics-tests}

`UranusLate.column_reaches_cycle_40` runs `run_hydro` on a Uranus column and requires exit code 0, no "Redoing the
step" and no "Terminating abnormally" in the log
([`test_uranus_cycle1_abort.cpp:115-127`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/tests/test_uranus_cycle1_abort.cpp#L115-L127), `column_reaches_cycle_40`).
That is the only snapy test that runs the kinetics block. There is no snapy test of one kinetics step's mass and
energy budget, of the evaporation rate or of `jupiter_evap_precip_1d`: **missing evidence** on the snapy side; the
rate law is tested in kintera. CPU only; no CUDA or multi-rank arm.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
Kinetics exists only in drivers that implement it. A user driver that calls only `forward` and `check_redo` has none.
:::

- First order in time, operator-split from the dynamics; the split error is not measured.
- No conserved limiter between the update and `check_redo` (`run_hydro.cpp:191-193`), so negative species from
  kinetics surface as a limiter repair at the next step ([chengcli/snapy#256](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/issues/256),
  #263).
- The update covers ghosts without an exchange.
- The evaporation note's status line ("not landed") is superseded: the extent law is present at the kintera pin.
- Not in the switch coverage matrix (@sec-ch12-matrix).
